name: Al-Anon
description: Support groups for families and friends of people with alcohol problems. 12-step program for loved ones affected by someone else's drinking.

sections.title: About Al-Anon Family Groups
sections.text: Al-Anon Family Groups is a worldwide fellowship of people who have been affected by someone else's drinking. Founded in 1951 by Lois Wilson and Anne B., wives of early Alcoholics Anonymous members, Al-Anon offers a program of recovery based on the Twelve Steps and Twelve Traditions. The organization helps families and friends of alcoholics find understanding, strength, and hope through shared experiences. Al-Anon is not affiliated with any religious organization, political group, or institution.

sections.title: Who Al-Anon Is For
sections.text: Al-Anon welcomes anyone whose life has been affected by someone else's drinking, whether that person is still drinking, has stopped, has passed away, or is no longer in their life. This includes spouses, partners, parents, children, siblings, friends, and coworkers. Alateen, a part of Al-Anon, is specifically for teenagers affected by a family member's drinking. You don't need to wait for someone to hit rock bottom or seek treatment—Al-Anon focuses on your own well-being regardless of what the drinker chooses to do.

sections.title: How Al-Anon Works
sections.text: Al-Anon meetings provide a safe, confidential environment where members share their experiences and learn from each other. The program centers on the Three Cs: You didn't Cause the alcoholism, you can't Cure it, and you can't Control it. Members learn to detach with love, set healthy boundaries, and focus on their own recovery. The Twelve Steps guide personal growth, while sponsors (experienced members) offer one-on-one support. Members discover they are not alone and that recovery is possible for them regardless of whether the alcoholic chooses to get help.

sections.title: Finding Al-Anon Meetings
sections.text: Al-Anon has over 24,000 groups meeting in 133 countries worldwide. Meetings are held in-person at community centers, churches, hospitals, and other locations, as well as online through Al-Anon's Electronic Meeting platform. To find meetings near you, visit al-anon.org and use the meeting finder tool. Meeting types include speaker meetings, discussion meetings, and step study groups. First-time visitors are always welcome—there's no registration or commitment required. Many groups welcome newcomers with special beginner meetings or literature.

sections.title: Getting Started with Al-Anon
sections.text: If you're new to Al-Anon, consider attending at least six different meetings before deciding if the program is right for you—each meeting has its own personality. Al-Anon has no dues or fees; groups are self-supporting through voluntary contributions. Free literature including pamphlets, books, and daily readers are available at meetings and through the Al-Anon website. The Al-Anon app provides meeting information, daily readings, and connection to the worldwide fellowship. Remember that everything shared at meetings is confidential.
